head: 08245cca98855e887be856cb625a3784ca59104a
claim: a maintainer can run one command on the lab Mac to soak a session for an hour through a display sleep and a client reconnect, and get a JSON timeline of fps and keystroke latency plus a reconnect clip; the run records that the picture and typing did not come back after the display wake until the client reconnected

target.version: desklink 0.5.14 engine at 08245cc on a MacBook Air (macOS 15.7.4, arm64)

steps.start: the lab Mac with a signed desklink-host, a headless Chrome client on the same Mac and an owned fixture window
steps: Opened a session through the bridge; the client showed the fixture (left cell pulsing, right cell flipping on keys)
Typed a marker every minute for one hour (60 markers, 240 keys), sampling frames and key-to-picture latency: timeline.json, summary.txt
Slept the display and woke it; the picture did not return and 3 markers (15 keys) never reached the Mac: timeline.json phase after-wake
Killed the client connection without telling the engine; reconnect-before-kill.png is the live fixture just before
Reconnected: reconnect-picture-back.png is the fixture back on screen after the reconnect; reconnect.webm is the clip across it
steps.result: The hour held 56 fps median and 49.8 ms median keystroke latency; after a display sleep and wake there was 0 fps and 15 of 15 keys lost until the client reconnected, then 55 fps and 61 ms median. System sleep was not exercised.

verdicts.seen: I read all three phase lines plus the recovery and cleanup lines. ok=true, markers=66. The after-wake phase before reconnect shows fps median 0 over 100 windows and 15 keys lost with null latency. After reconnect, fps median is 55 and first echo is 82 ms. Cleanup is 7/7 and power settings are restored. This matches the outcome that picture and typing did not return after wake until the client reconnected.

I read the whole JSON object. ok is true and failure is null. The after-wake phase shows fps windows 100, median 0, and latency samples 0 with lost 15. The recovery block shows wake_first_frame_ms 60230, which the summary notes means none arrived within the 60000 ms wait. Reconnect_first_frame_ms is 2315. Events run sleep-requested, woke, client-killed, reconnected. All 7 cleanup steps are ok and sleep_settings_restored is true. A timeline path is given, but no reconnect clip appears in this text, so the clip part is not shown here.
